statement: From Contours generates a TIN terrain from selected contour lines at different heights as a group.
superiority: Constrained Delaunay with breaklines and robust handling of contour gaps.
notes: Acceptance sketch: 20 contour rings at known z; TIN vertices equal contour points; no overhangs; interpolated heights within 1 percent.

statement: From Scratch creates a flat rectangular TIN grid with specified size and spacing.
superiority: Arbitrary boundaries and adaptive spacing.
notes: Acceptance sketch: 10x10 m at 1 m spacing: 100 cells, 200 triangles.

statement: Smoove raises or lowers selected TIN vertices with a soft radius and typed offset.
superiority: Brush falloff curves and undo preview.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Raise a 2 m radius by 1 m: center displacement 1 m, falloff monotone.

statement: Add Detail subdivides TIN triangles at a clicked edge or face to add vertices.
superiority: Adaptive refinement with error bounds.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Added vertex count and positions as expected.

statement: Flip Edge swaps the shared diagonal of two triangles to remove flat areas.
superiority: A Delaunay flip optimizer fixes whole regions in one click instead of edge-by-edge flipping.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Flip an edge in a 5x5 TIN; the result remains a valid triangulation with no overlaps and the same boundary.

statement: Stamp imprints a footprint of a building onto terrain with a typed flat zone and slope margin.
superiority: Cut and fill volumes reported.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Stamp 10x10 pad with 2 m margin; pad flat to 1e-9.

statement: Drape projects edges, text or imagery onto terrain.
superiority: Drape works onto NURBS surfaces and meshes, not only TINs, with a user-set projection direction.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Draped edges lie on the TIN surface within 1e-9 and their plan projection equals the source.

statement: Terrain from Add Location can be shown or hidden.
superiority: Terrain state can be saved per scene so context can be shown in some views and hidden in others.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Toggle visibility; terrain group hidden flag changes and the drawing output omits the terrain.

statement: Add Location selects a region on a map, imports imagery tiles and optional terrain, and geolocates the model.

source.ref: Add Location (geolocate with map and terrain)

superiority: Multiple imagery and elevation providers selectable.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/site-context-add-location Acceptance sketch: Import a known region; model latitude/longitude equals chosen within 1e-6 degree.

statement: Imagery tiles of 256x256 are merged into larger .skm materials with limits set by graphics hardware.

source.ref: Add Location: imagery to materials (.skm tiles)

superiority: Streaming imagery tiles with LOD.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Imported tile mosaic aligned within one pixel.

statement: Add Location can geolocate using a CRS (EPSG code or calibration file .dc/.jxl) with Project Base Point; CRS not changeable after use; stored in .skp as IFC data.
superiority: Full PROJ-based transformation with datum shifts and grid files.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Geolocate with EPSG:2263 and base point; coordinates convert with sub-millimetre agreement to reference proj library.

statement: Model Info Location panel shows and clears latitude, longitude, north angle, and country.
superiority: Separates true north and project north explicitly and shows both in the dialog.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/geolocation-sketchup Acceptance sketch: Edit latitude and longitude; shadow direction at a fixed instant moves to the recomputed solar position.

statement: North angle and clearing geolocation data.
superiority: Named north references with project north and true north both stored and converted.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/geolocation-sketchup Acceptance sketch: Set north angle 20 degrees; solar azimuth results rotate by exactly 20 degrees; clear geolocation removes location data.

statement: USGS DEM and SDTS import to a TIN with point count control and gradient texture.
superiority: GeoTIFF, LAS and tiled elevation with streaming.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Import sample DEM; elevations at control points within 0.5 m of source.

statement: Preexisting terrain can be imported and geolocated.
superiority: Direct coordinate import.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Terrain aligned to coordinates.

statement: Modeling terrain and other rounded shapes using Sandbox.

source.ref: Create terrain from scratch workflow (organic shapes)

superiority: Subdivision-surface terrain gives smooth organic shapes with exact control points, not a fixed TIN grid.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Build a rounded mound from a grid; surface height at the center equals the specified value within 1 mm.

statement: Delete Add Location imagery.
superiority: Imagery layers are individually removable and re-orderable without touching geometry.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Delete imported imagery; imagery materials are removed, terrain geometry and its vertex count are unchanged.

statement: Estimating height from shadows or camera.
superiority: Height estimation from imagery and shadows with a stated uncertainty rather than a single value.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Estimate height of a 10 m fixture from shadow length at a known sun angle; result within 3 percent.

statement: Add Location in web and iPad clients.

source.ref: Site context in SketchUp Web and iPad

superiority: One imagery and terrain pipeline serves desktop, web and iPad so results are identical on every client.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/add-location-sketchup-desktop-0 Acceptance sketch: Run Add Location for the same region on desktop and web; terrain vertex heights agree within 1 cm.

statement: Extension exporting SketchUp geometry to Trimble Siteworks machine-ready design files and importing field points.
superiority: Direct LandXML and machine control exports.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/site-contractor-extension-getting-started Acceptance sketch: Export surface; reimport; deviations under 1 mm.

statement: Revit Importer imports .rvt views with metadata, phases, materials.
superiority: Native RVT through licensed route.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/importing-revit-metadata https://help.sketchup.com/en/revit-phases-sketchup Acceptance sketch: Import sample RVT; element counts and metadata equal source.
